problems.title: Recognise a cube in the numerator
problems.question: Evaluate[7.3³+3·7.3²·2.7+3·7.3·2.7²+2.7³]/(5.5²−4.5²).
problems.idea: Look for a standard identity or a short chain of geometric facts.
steps: The value is 10³/(1·10)=100.

problems.title: Rectangle sides preserve directions
problems.question: Two rectangles have vertices on a vertical line; the upper marked angle is 40°, the lower30°. Find the marked crossing angle.
problems.idea: Look for a standard identity or a short chain of geometric facts.
formulas: Opposite rectangle sides are parallel and adjacent sides perpendicular.
steps: The rising side at the crossing makes90°−40°=50° with the rightward horizontal.
The descending side makes90°−30°=60° below that horizontal. The marked right-side angle is 50°+60°=110°.

problems.title: Multiply price and quantity factors
problems.question: Apples initially cost10 GEL. Later their unit price falls20%, and Nino buys30% more weight. What is the new cost?
problems.idea: Look for a standard identity or a short chain of geometric facts.
steps: The product is 10.4 GEL.

problems.title: Count roots of nested absolute values
problems.question: How many roots has||x−6|−6|=4?
problems.idea: Look for a standard identity or a short chain of geometric facts.
formulas: Letu=|x−6|. Then|u−6|=4 givesu=10 or 2.
steps: The roots are −4,16,4,8, four distinct values.

problems.title: Distance to the horizontal axis
problems.question: Find the distance from the intersection of y=4x−8 and 3x−2y=1 to Ox.
problems.idea: Look for a standard identity or a short chain of geometric facts.
formulas: Distance from(x, y) to Ox is|y|.
steps: Substitute to obtain3x−2(4x−8)=1, so x=3, y=4.
The requested distance is 4.

problems.title: A sixty-degree chord equals the radius
problems.question: A length-24 segment is split by a circle into consecutive parts in ratio1:2:3. The middle chord subtends60° at the centre. Find the diameter.
problems.idea: Look for a standard identity or a short chain of geometric facts.
formulas: The ratio unit is 24/6=4, so the middle chord is 8. A60° central triangle is equilateral.
steps: The chord therefore equals the radius 8. The diameter is 16.

problems.title: Use the extra coordinate condition
problems.question: Find the point on y=2x−3 whose ordinate is 7 less than its abscissa.
problems.idea: Look for a standard identity or a short chain of geometric facts.
formulas: The condition is y=x−7.
steps: Set2x−3=x−7 to obtainx=−4. Then y=−11.

problems.title: Compare the coefficient of x
problems.question: If x²−8x+15=(x+a)(x+b), find|a+b|.
problems.idea: Look for a standard identity or a short chain of geometric facts.
formulas: Expansion givesx²+(a+b)x+ab.
steps: Thus a+b=−8 and its absolute value is 8.

problems.title: An injective linear function has equal inputs
problems.question: For f(x)=4x−7, solve f(2x−1)=f(x+5).
problems.idea: Look for a standard identity or a short chain of geometric facts.
formulas: Because the slope is nonzero, equal function values require equal arguments.
steps: Thus2x−1=x+5, givingx=6.

problems.title: Parallel line with a specified intercept
problems.question: Find the line parallel to 3x−5y+7=0 with y-intercept−3.
problems.idea: Look for a standard identity or a short chain of geometric facts.
formulas: The original slope is 3/5=0.6.
steps: Keeping that slope and using the given intercept givesy=0.6x−3.

problems.title: Maximise two bounded fractions
problems.question: Find the maximum of 14/(9x²−12xy+4y²+7)+12/(|5x−3y−1|+3).
problems.idea: Look for a standard identity or a short chain of geometric facts.
formulas: The denominators are(3x−2y)²+7≥7 and|5x−3y−1|+3≥3.
steps: The terms are at most2 and 4, so the sum is at most6.
Equality requires3x−2y=0 and 5x−3y−1=0. These give x=2, y=3, so 6 is attained.

problems.title: Tangent lengths and a semiperimeter
problems.question: An incircle touches AB at M, MB=6, and triangle ABC has perimeter42. Find AC.
problems.idea: Look for a standard identity or a short chain of geometric facts.
formulas: Equal tangent segments give semiperimeter s=AM+BM+(tangent length from C).
steps: Here s=21. SideAC consists of the tangent lengths from A and C, so AC=s−BM=21−6=15.

problems.title: Arc ratios determine an incenter angle
problems.question: The consecutive arcs AB, BC, CA have ratio1:5:6. Q is the incenter of triangle ABC. Find AQC.
problems.idea: Look for a standard identity or a short chain of geometric facts.
formulas: The arcs sum to 360°, so their unit is 30°. ArcCA avoiding B is 180°, making B=90°.
steps: The incenter identity gives AQC=90°+B/2=90°+45°=135°.

problems.title: Combine an inscribed angle and an isosceles radius triangle
problems.question: In the printed circle diagram, the top inscribed angle is 63° and the lower-right angle between radius and chord is 63°. Find the marked left angle.
problems.idea: Look for a standard identity or a short chain of geometric facts.
formulas: Label the left/right diameter endpoints L, R, the upper point T, the lower point U, and lower-right point V.
steps: AngleLTV=63° gives arc LUV=126°. In triangle OUV, the equal radii make its two base angles63°, so arc UV=180°−126°=54°.
Thus arc LU=126°−54°=72°. The lower semicircle is 180°, so arc UR=108°.
The marked angle ULR is half arc UR, namely54°.

problems.title: An exterior triangle angle from intersecting lines
problems.question: In the printed diagram, D, B, C, E are collinear, A, F, B collinear, D, F, G collinear, A, G, C collinear. A=20°, D=10°, BFG=140°. Find ACE.
problems.idea: Look for a standard identity or a short chain of geometric facts.
formulas: The line DG rises10° above the base. The acute angle between AB and DG is 180°−140°=40°.
steps: ThusAB rises10°+40°=50°. Since the angle between AB and AC at A is 20°, AC rises70° above the base.
The requested exterior angle ACE is 70°.

problems.title: Transfer an angle between tangents to a second circle
problems.question: In the printed two-circle diagram, the small-circle tangent rays enclose an outer arc200°. A chord crossing in the large circle gives 70°. Find its marked lower arc.
problems.idea: Look for a standard identity or a short chain of geometric facts.
formulas: LetA be the large circle’s left point, B its upper-right point, D its lower-right point, and C the lower-left point. AD is a diameter.
steps: The small circle’s other arc is 160°, so the angle between the two tangent lines is(200°−160°)/2=20°. This is angle BAD.
Thus arc BD=40°. The chord-crossing70° angle gives(arc AC+arc BD)/2=70°, so arc AC=100°.
The lower semicircle AD measures180°. Therefore the marked arc CD is 180°−100°=80°.

problems.title: Equal arcs and a perpendicular to a diameter
problems.question: In the printed circle diagram, the two upper arcs are equal, the right angle on the upper triangle is 36°, and the top segment is perpendicular to a diameter. Find the top marked angle.
problems.idea: Look for a standard identity or a short chain of geometric facts.
formulas: Label the upper triangle A, B, C from left to top to right, and the opposite diameter endpoint D.
steps: AngleACB=36° gives arc AB=72°, and the equal marked arc BC is also72°.
The upper semicircle DC has 180°, so arc DA=180°−144°=36°. Thus arc DB=108° and angle DCB=54°.
The top segment is perpendicular to DC, so its angle with BC is 90°−54°=36°.

problems.title: Compare the hypotenuse median with a right-angle bisector
problems.question: In a right triangle, the bisector and median from the right-angle vertex make23°. Find the larger acute angle.
problems.idea: Look for a standard identity or a short chain of geometric facts.
formulas: The bisector is 45° from either leg. The hypotenuse median makes an angle with a leg equal to one of the triangle’s acute angles.
steps: That acute angle is 45°±23°, namely22° or 68°. The two acute angles are therefore22° and 68°.

problems.title: Mix two metal ratios
problems.question: The zinc:copper ratios in two alloys are 5:2 and 3:4. How much of the first alloy is needed for 28kg of a 50%-zinc mixture?
problems.idea: Look for a standard identity or a short chain of geometric facts.
formulas: If the first mass is m, the zinc balance is(5/7)m+(3/7)(28−m)=14.
steps: Multiply by 7:5m+84−3m=98. Hence2m=14 and m=7kg.

problems.title: Find a parallel graph by its slope
problems.question: Which listed graph is parallel to the line through A(1,4), B(−3,0)?
problems.idea: Look for a standard identity or a short chain of geometric facts.
steps: The listed line y=x−2 has slope1 and is parallel to the given line.

problems.title: A right triangle’s hypotenuse is its circumdiameter
problems.question: Triangle angles have ratio2:7:9, and its largest side is 8. Find circumradius.
problems.idea: Look for a standard identity or a short chain of geometric facts.
formulas: The angle unit is 180°/18=10°, so the largest angle is 90°.
steps: The largest side is the hypotenuse8. Its circumradius is half that length,4.

problems.title: Recover a count ratio from score totals
problems.question: Girls’ average score is 20% higher than boys’, but boys’ total is 60% higher than girls’. How many percent more boys participated?
problems.idea: Look for a standard identity or a short chain of geometric facts.
formulas: Total=count×average. If boys’ average is b, girls’ average is 1.2b.
steps: ThenN_b b=1.6N_g(1.2b), so N_b/N_g=1.92.
The excess count is 92%.

problems.title: Smallest distinct composite summands
problems.question: Find the smallest sum of three distinct composite positive integers.
problems.idea: Look for a standard identity or a short chain of geometric facts.
formulas: The three smallest composites are 4,6,8.
steps: Their sum is 18, and choosing any larger composite can only increase it.

problems.title: A prime divisibility condition fixes two positive integers
problems.question: Positive integersx, y satisfy xy+200=(y+1)². Find x+y.
problems.idea: Look for a standard identity or a short chain of geometric facts.
formulas: Rearrange to y(x−y−2)=−199. Since199 is prime, the positive divisory is 1 or 199.
steps: If y=1, then x=−196, not positive. Ify=199, then x−199−2=−1, so x=200.
The sum is 200+199=399.

problems.title: Singular coefficients are not enough for infinite solutions
problems.question: For whichk does4x−3y=15+kx, x+2y=5k−kx have infinitely many solutions?
problems.idea: Look for a standard identity or a short chain of geometric facts.
formulas: Write(4−k)x−3y=15,(1+k)x+2y=5k. Proportional coefficients require2(4−k)+3(1+k)=0.
steps: This givesk=−11. The first coefficient row is then−3/2 times the second.
But the constants15 and −55 do not have this ratio:15≠(−3/2)(−55). Thus the equations are inconsistent even at the only singular value.
